title: FCA and Bank of England set out shared vision for tokenisation in UK wholesale markets
key_claim: The Bank of England commits to enabling tokenised equivalents of assets that are already eligible to be used as collateral at central counterparties and in its own central bank operations, alongside a live synchronisation service targeted for 2028, a consultation on extending RTGS and CHAPS settlement hours towards near 24x7, and PRA Dear CEO letters on the prudential treatment of tokenised asset exposures.
frame_summary: Argues that the UK can unlock tokenisation by giving firms regulatory certainty inside the existing perimeter, treating tokenised instruments as the same instruments rather than as a new asset class needing a new regime.
verbatim_quote: working to enable tokenised equivalents of already eligible assets to be used as collateral both at central counterparties and in its own central bank operations
verbatim_list: The Bank of England has published a consultation on extending RTGS and CHAPS settlement hours, setting out next steps towards near 24/7 settlement.

The Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) has published Dear CEO letters setting out updated guidance on the prudential treatment of tokenised asset exposures and on innovations in deposits, e-money and stablecoins.
notes: Primary anchor for the perimeter condition: eligibility is extended to tokenised forms of assets that are already eligible, not to natively on-chain assets. Also the single document tying the collateral question to the settlement-hours question.

title: Extending RTGS and CHAPS settlement hours: next steps towards near 24x7 settlement
key_claim: The Bank proposes weekend and bank holiday RTGS/CHAPS settlement no earlier than 2029 and 22-hour weekday settlement no earlier than 2031, building on an early morning extension opening CHAPS at 01:30 from September 2027, and states that extended hours would have wider consequences for the prudential liquidity risk framework and the PRA's approach to setting intraday liquidity requirements, to be communicated in due course. Responses closed on 10 August 2026.
frame_summary: Argues that near 24x7 central bank settlement is the right direction of travel for innovation, cross-border payments and liquidity efficiency, while conceding that the liquidity and prudential consequences have not yet been worked out.
verbatim_quote: Extending CHAPS settlement hours would have wider consequences for the prudential liquidity risk framework, including regulatory liquidity reporting and the PRA’s approach to setting intraday liquidity requirements.
verbatim_list: Building on the already-announced early morning extension that will see CHAPS open at 01:30 (instead of 06:00) from September 2027, in this paper we outline next steps to extend RTGS/CHAPS settlement hours and advance towards our ambition of near 24x7 settlement.
Our initial preferred option is to introduce an additional settlement day on the weekend, most likely on Sundays, and certain bank holidays, no earlier than 2029.
After that, we would propose to extend settlement hours to 22 hours per day (Monday to Friday and one day at the weekend), no earlier than 2031, which will deliver further benefits.
notes: Supplies the settlement-hours half of the mismatch and the Bank's own acknowledgement that the intraday liquidity framework is unresolved.

publisher: European Central Bank (Financial Integration and Structure)
title: The role of the Eurosystem in the scaling-up of a tokenised financial ecosystem
key_claim: From 30 March 2026 the Eurosystem accepts marketable assets issued in central securities depositories using DLT-based services as eligible collateral, provided they are available for settlement in TARGET2-Securities, so the mobilisation process is identical to that for any other marketable asset. Euro-denominated debt instruments with digital exposure stood at around EUR 2 billion at end-2025, and the Pontes pilot launches in the third quarter of 2026.
frame_summary: Argues that the Eurosystem should support tokenisation by extending existing collateral and settlement arrangements to DLT-issued assets, keeping central bank money and the CSD layer as the anchor rather than allowing a parallel infrastructure to form.
verbatim_quote: As a result, the mobilisation process is the same as that for any other marketable asset accepted by the Eurosystem.
verbatim_list: From 30 March 2026 the Eurosystem accepts marketable assets issued in CSDs using DLT-based services as eligible collateral for Eurosystem credit operations.

According to Bloomberg data, at the end of 2025 the amount outstanding of euro-denominated debt instruments with some digital exposure, including but not limited to assets issued using DLT, stood at around €2 billion (Chart A).
It will enable the settlement of tokenised financial instruments in central bank money, with a pilot phase to be launched as of the third quarter of 2026.
notes: Structural anchor. The canonical statement of the perimeter condition from the euro-area side, and the source of the scale figure that frames how small the tokenised collateral pool still is.

title: The path to the next-generation monetary and financial system lies in safeguarding trust in money
key_claim: The BIS Annual Economic Report 2026 special chapter argues that tokenisation should be brought into the existing two-tier system, where central banks provide the monetary anchor and commercial banks provide services to the public, and that innovation delivers benefits when anchored in sound institutional arrangements, consistent legal frameworks and strong supervision.
frame_summary: Argues that the safe route for tokenisation is absorption into the existing two-tier monetary architecture under a unified ledger, not the construction of a parallel settlement system outside it.
verbatim_quote: financial innovation can deliver significant benefits when it is anchored in sound institutional arrangements, consistent legal frameworks and strong supervision
notes: Establishes that the absorb-into-the-existing-system posture is the international standard-setter's position, not a UK or euro-area idiosyncrasy.

publisher: Association for Financial Markets in Europe (AFME)
title: Consultation Response: FCA and Bank of England Call for Input on the Future of Tokenisation
date_evidence:
Consultation Response
FCA and Bank of England Call for Input on 
the Future of Tokenisation
3 July 2026
key_claim: AFME, representing over 150 banks, identifies collateral mobility as the clearest near-term commercial opportunity in tokenisation, citing global DLT repo transactions averaging $384bn daily, warns that a synchronisation capability targeted for 2028 may be too slow if tokenised assets scale earlier, and flags that the Basel SCO60 classification can push otherwise low-risk exposures into Group 2b at a 1,250% risk weight.
frame_summary: Argues that the UK authorities' vision is directionally right but too slow and too cautious, and that unless tokenised and non-tokenised forms of the same asset are treated identically the market will fragment liquidity and trap collateral rather than release it.
verbatim_quote: we see one of the clearest and most actionable, commercial opportunities in the use of fungible tokenised securities as collateral across CCPs, uncleared OTC derivatives and central bank operations
verbatim_list: Tokenisation offers significant potential for greater efficiencies and faster and more precise movement in collateral and repo markets, with global DLT repo transactions averaging $384bn on a daily basis.
However, a synchronisation capability targeted for 2028 may be too slow if tokenised assets and private settlement solutions scale earlier.

The binary classification approach based on DLT design and archetype can create a “cliff effect” whereby otherwise low-risk exposures may fall into Group 2b and attract a 1,250% risk weight, making underwriting and market activity uneconomical.

The benefits should also be weighed against additional costs, including pre-positioning liquidity to meet atomic settlement demand and extended hours for risk management and oversight, in addition to ensuring operational resilience and smart-contract integrity.
notes: The market-side voice and the principal counter-argument source: the sell-side case is that the mobilisation gap is a sequencing problem the authorities are creating, not an inherent feature of tokenisation.

title: Who stands behind tokenised money?
key_claim: Atomic settlement reduces principal risk but raises intraday liquidity demand, because settling gross in real time ties up more cash than deferred netting, and always-on execution can synchronise withdrawals, margin calls and collateral sales.
frame_summary: Argues that the substantive question in tokenisation is which balance sheet stands behind final payment, and that speed and atomicity are not improvements in themselves because they shift risk into liquidity and operational channels.
verbatim_quote: Atomic settlement reduces principal risk. It also raises intraday liquidity demand because settling gross in real time ties up more cash than deferred netting. Always-on execution can synchronise withdrawals, margin calls and collateral sales.
notes: Supplies the mechanism linking always-on settlement to a higher intraday liquidity requirement, independently of the UK and euro-area policy documents.

publisher: Bank of England (RTGS CHAPS Industry Forum)
title: Summary of the RTGS CHAPS Industry Forum
key_claim: At the first meeting of the Bank's RTGS CHAPS Industry Forum on 4 June 2026, members agreed near 24/7 settlement was the right direction but said the risks were large and the industry impact significant; the effect of the change programme on liquidity management was deferred to a future meeting. The roadmap places further extension of settlement hours in 2028 and beyond.
frame_summary: Argues, from the participant side, that the direction of travel towards near 24/7 settlement is correct but that the operational, cultural and liquidity-management consequences for banks have not yet been worked through.
verbatim_quote: There was significant discussion around the level of change both RTGS and other change initiatives would require across industry, the need for participants to respond to this, including via changes to business and operating models, as well as the impact that these changes could have on liquidity management, which will be a topic for a future meeting.
verbatim_list: They confirmed that extending hours near 24/7 was the right direction of travel, but noted that risks were large, and the impact to industry was significant.
notes: Evidence that the liquidity-management consequence of extended hours is a known but explicitly deferred question, in the Bank's own minutes.
